annotation.title_clean: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.title_en: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kanade, T. M.; Y, H.; Pulekar, D.; Savale, T. K.; Kamble, S. M.
annotation.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research and Scientific Studies
annotation.summary_en: Mixed-method study by Indian authors (industrial and logistics case studies, expert surveys and interviews) on giving IoT-enabled robots "citizenship-like responsibilities". It weighs productivity against accountability. It concludes that this raises ethical, legal and societal questions and calls for accountability frameworks to be built into robot design.
key_provisions_or_claims: IoT-enabled robots outperform humans on consistency, scalability and energy efficiency
More autonomy does not always mean better performance; algorithms and operational protocols need refining
Accountability mechanisms aid transparency but currently do little for task efficiency
Citizenship-like responsibilities for robots challenge traditional frameworks of responsibility and agency
Calls for multidisciplinary integration of ethics and accountability frameworks into robot design and deployment
